header:
Date: 2026-05-07 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rohan Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Synergia CTO), Ethan Park (Synergia Platform Eng), Amira Hassan (Synergia DevOps)
Location: Zoom
summary: Initial integration discovery exploring Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for Synergia's gateway/proxy architecture. Focus on SDK language support, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, rate limiting/quotas per tenant, VPC peering and observability hooks. Agreement to run a pilot and follow up with technical deep-dive and sample configs.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Gateway/proxy placement and sidecar vs centralized
Rate limits, quotas and burst handling
Observability: Prometheus/OTel/tracing and token-level cost breakdown
Security: VPC peering, KMS, SOC2, SSO
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're Maya from Redwood, AE, and Rohan our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Laura Kim: Good thanks, busy day but excited.
[00:12] Ethan Park: Hi all. Quick note, apologies if audio drops, we're on a VPN that sometimes...
[00:20] Maya Chen: No worries. Agenda — quick intro, high-level product map (hosted, dedicated, private), then Rohan will dig into integration patterns with your gateway/proxy and LangChain flow, then Q&A.
[00:33] Amira Hassan: Sounds good. For context, we run a central API gateway that handles tenancy and auth, then fan-out to multiple microservices. We're evaluating putting LLM calls behind our gateway or as a sidecar per service. I want to understand latency impact and the ops model.
[00:49] Rohan Patel: Right, that's a common pattern. Two main options: centralized proxy/gateway that forwards to Redwood, or sidecar/adaptor embedded in the service using the SDK. Tradeoffs are latency vs manageability. With a sidecar you can do local KV cache and prefix caching which helps token cost, but increases deployment surface.
[01:10] Laura Kim: We're particularly concerned about rate limits — we have bursty traffic from our search UI during peak. Can Redwood do per-tenant quotas and per-route throttling?
[01:18] Maya Chen: Yes, on Hosted we have flexible per-api-key quotas and rate-limiting. For Dedicated and Private you can enforce at your VPC edge or via our routing policies too. We support quotas at token-level and request-level and can do burst buckets and leaky bucket behavior.
[01:34] Ethan Park: How deterministic are those? We need to guarantee SLAs for paying customers.
[01:38] Rohan Patel: On Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools so throughput is predictable. Hosted has fair-share and tiered capacity; we can set reserved lanes for your account in hosted with burst credits. For Private, you’re in full control — peering, KMS, and you manage capacity.
[01:55] Amira Hassan: Can you describe the VPC peering flow? We have strict egress rules and need private connectivity.
[02:02] Maya Chen: For Redwood Private we offer a managed control plane and a customer VPC peering option. Traffic can stay on the private network, we support strict IP allowlists and mutual TLS. Our on-prem option can be air-gapped if needed.
[02:18] Laura Kim: Any requirements for certificates or our PKI?
[02:22] Rohan Patel: We can support customer-managed certs; we also integrate with KMS/HSM for model keys and audit logs. We'll send the exact network and firewall requirements in the follow-up.
[02:33] [00:03:00] Ethan Park: On SDKs, what languages and features? We use Python for inference pipelines and Node for web. We also rely heavily on LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors.
[03:40] Rohan Patel: We have first-class SDKs for Python and Node, plus a lightweight HTTP client. The Python SDK has direct LangChain integration helpers — prompt templates, streaming tokens, and function call glue. For LlamaIndex we provide a connector that can be used as a retriever; it wraps our embeddings API and can stream back results. Note: the auto-generated LlamaIndex name in some docs might show as 'LlamaIdx' — apologies for mismatch.
[04:05] Laura Kim: Do you support async streaming responses and token-level callbacks for cost accounting?
[04:12] Rohan Patel: Yes, streaming is supported in SDKs and the HTTP API. You can subscribe to token events, or we can provide post-request token accounting via webhooks. We also have per-token cost export in the console and via our usage API.
[04:26] Amira Hassan: For the gateway approach, we'd want a proxy that can do request shaping and apply caching. Any reference architecture?
[04:33] Rohan Patel: Common pattern is a lightweight proxy service that handles auth, enforces quotas and caching, and forwards enriched requests to Redwood. We have an example sidecar and a centralized proxy repo — we'll share links. Important to consider KV cache (prefix caching) which lives in the sidecar usually to avoid cache stampede and reduce tokens.
[04:52] [00:06:00] Laura Kim: Observability — we need traces correlated from our services to Redwood calls. Do you emit spans or support trace context propagation?
[06:08] Rohan Patel: We support trace context headers (W3C traceparent) and export spans to OTLP. You can ingest them into Honeycomb/Lightstep/Datadog. Also export metrics via Prometheus endpoint for latency, tokens/second, model-level throughput. We'll add an example OTel config.
[06:30] Ethan Park: Do you do sampling? We can't ship 100% of spans.
[06:35] Rohan Patel: Yes, we support adaptive sampling and you can set sampling rates per route. Also you can request raw logs/audit streams for security reviews.
[06:45] [00:09:00] Maya Chen: Quick interjection — Laura, can you remind us of timeline and success criteria?
[07:51] Laura Kim: Timeline: PoC in 6 weeks, production in Q3. Success: throughput under 50ms p95 for short chats, cost below our internal threshold, and SOC2 compliance for logs.
[07:58] Maya Chen: Good, that's feasible. We'll propose a short pilot to validate latency and our integration patterns.
[08:05] Amira Hassan: About ACLs and tenant isolation — we want per-customer data partitioning, separate embeddings storage for sensitive tenants.
[08:14] Rohan Patel: We support per-tenant keys and separate model contexts. On Dedicated and Private you can choose encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS. For embeddings we can segregate storage by namespace; we'll document retention and deletion flows.
[08:33] [00:12:00] Ethan Park: Security review — will you provide SOC2 and ISO docs, plus a penetration test report?
[09:39] Maya Chen: Yes, SOC2 and ISO are in our compliance pack. Pen test summary is available, full reports under NDA. We'll send the security packet after the call.
[09:51] Laura Kim: Regarding rate limiting, if a tenant exceeds quota, what's the behavior? Soft failures, 429s, or fallback to cheaper model?
[10:00] Rohan Patel: Configurable. You can choose strict 429s, queueing with backpressure, or automated fallback to a smaller model variant with a warning header. We can also configure burst credits per tenant.
[10:18] Amira Hassan: We want the gateway to tag requests with tenant-id and plan. Is there a secure header we should use?
[10:24] Rohan Patel: Use a signed JWT in the header; we validate signature. For Private you can do mTLS between proxy and Redwood runtime.
[10:33] [00:15:00] Ethan Park: On model variants — can you do A/B rollouts and canary?
[11:40] Rohan Patel: Yes, rollouts are supported. You can define traffic splits per route, automatic rollback on error thresholds, and experiment buckets. We'll show console screenshots.
[11:52] Laura Kim: Good. For LangChain integration, do you have example chains for reranking and conversational retrieval?
[12:01] Rohan Patel: We do. We have sample repos: one for streaming conversational retrieval with LlamaIndex + our embeddings, and one for rerank pipelines. We'll share code snippets. Small heads up: some sample notebooks still reference older API names, so expect minor diffs.
[12:20] [00:18:00] Amira Hassan: How do you handle prompt guardrails and red-teaming for hallucinations?
[13:28] Rohan Patel: Two levers: model selection and post-processing. We have safety filters, toxins detection, and you can run local evals on a test set. Also the console has quality alerts tied to eval prompt sets so you can detect regressions.
[13:44] Ethan Park: For billing, can we get detailed token-level billing per-route and per-tenant exported to our billing system?
[13:52] Maya Chen: Yes, we provide per-token usage exports, per-route tagging, and a usage API. You can pull hourly aggregates to reconcile invoices. We also support rate-limited webhooks for usage events.
[14:08] [00:21:00] Laura Kim: Performance tests — we'd like Redwood to run a bench with our typical payloads. How do we set that up?
[15:20] Rohan Patel: We'll need a request profile: qps, payload sizes, sequence length distribution, and concurrency. With Dedicated we can provision a bench cluster in our staging to mirror production. For Hosted we'd run synthetic runs in our environment but can reserve capacity.
[15:40] Laura Kim: We also use LlamaIndex heavy retrieval — embeddings size and throughput matter. We may need quantized models on GPU.
[15:50] Rohan Patel: We can recommend quantization profiles and model variants. For embeddings throughput we have batching knobs and an async embedding pipeline. We'll include config suggestions.
[16:04] [00:24:00] Amira Hassan: Observability hooks — how do we correlate tokens to traces without leaking PII?
[17:12] Rohan Patel: We emit opaque request IDs and allow you to enrich traces with metadata in your sidecar before sending. We avoid including prompt text in traces by default; you can opt-in for debug captures under strict controls.
[17:31] Ethan Park: Any existing customers with similar setups?
[17:36] Maya Chen: Yes, we've onboarded a few search platforms and an e-commerce customer with centralized gateway + sidecar. We'll anonymize case studies and share architecture diagrams.
[17:50] [00:27:00] Laura Kim: If we go Private, what's the support model? On-call, SLAs?
[19:01] Maya Chen: Private comes with an enterprise support tier, 24/7 on-call for critical incidents depending on SLA. There's also an onboarding week with SE to tune performance.
[19:18] Amira Hassan: We might prefer Dedicated for initial pilot to avoid network teams' long review cycles.
[19:24] Rohan Patel: That's common — Dedicated gives predictability and less network ops friction. Then you can migrate to Private later.
[19:33] [00:30:00] Ethan Park: About the proxy — can we run Redwood runtime in our VPC with network egress blocked except to our services?
[20:45] Rohan Patel: Yes, our Private runtime can be deployed with strict egress rules and you can host model weights on-prem for air-gapped mode. We'll include a top-level deployment diagram.
[20:58] Laura Kim: Ops — how are updates managed for Private deploys? Do you push changes or do we control upgrades?
[21:10] Rohan Patel: We typically do a customer-scheduled upgrade. There's a control plane patch for telemetry but runtime upgrades are scheduled with customer approval.
[21:22] [00:33:00] Amira Hassan: About quotas enforcement — do you have a middleware lib we can drop into the gateway?
[22:30] Rohan Patel: Yes, we have a middleware for popular gateways (Envoy, Kong) and an example Express/Koa plugin for Node. We'll send the repo link.
[22:45] Laura Kim: Any pitfalls you recommend avoiding?
[22:51] Rohan Patel: Watch for unbounded streaming and long-running sessions that hold KV cache slots; also aggressive batching can increase tail latency if not tuned. Also pay attention to tokenization mismatches across SDKs.
[23:10] [00:36:00] Maya Chen: Good points. Quick recap and next steps?
[24:18] Laura Kim: Recap: we want sample proxy config, LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, security pack, and a bench plan. PoC in 6 weeks.
[24:28] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll send materials and propose a date for the SE deep-dive.
[24:34] Amira Hassan: One last thing — our legal wants to know data retention defaults.
[24:40] Maya Chen: Default retention is 30 days for logs, embeddings retention configurable per-account. We'll include retention policy doc.
[24:47] [00:39:00] Ethan Park: Alright thanks — we'll collate internal stakeholders and share traffic profile.
[25:02] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet.
[25:07] Laura Kim: Thanks, talk soon.
[00:52:10] End of recording. Notes: minor transcript glitches around proprietary names (LlamaIndex vs LlamaIdx).
